items.evidence: Notes do not mention the project manager opening the meeting or stating the agenda.

'75% of 100 subjects found remotes ugly; 80% willing to pay more', 'Losing the remote', 'Too many buttons', 'most common actions are channel and volume changes', 'Desire for voice recognition inversely related to age'. Speaker not named but content is all there.

'Remote is a communication device: user input -> chip -> infrared signal -> TV receiver' covers how a remote works; nothing on the design approach (design specs, prototypes, user feedback, conventional vs novel).
The two example remotes (fully featured vs basic) and their pros and cons are not in the notes.
'Four core components: Energy source, Chip, User interface, Infrared bulb' plus the signal path.
Notes cover new requirements (teletext, TV only, corporate identity), target group, voice recognition ruled out, find-it locator, battery/cradle.
'each team member to complete a questionnaire and summary'.
'then 30 minutes individual work'.
'Upload presentations to shared project folder' but nothing about the project manager posting the minutes and project documentation.
'Upload presentations to shared project folder' as a next step for the group.
'components concept (ID)'.
'user interface concept' listed but owner (user interface designer) not stated.
'market trend watching' listed but owner (marketing expert) not stated.
'no teletext (superseded by internet)'.
'Scope confirmed: TV only, no video or other devices'.
'Corporate identity: yellow and black color scheme ... must be visible in final design'.
'Core emphasis: simplicity and fashion'.

'age segmentation less useful than lifestyle/attitude targeting' captures dropping age targeting, but does not say the team chose to define objectives (fashion, simplicity) instead; also says 'roughly under 65'.
'Find-it locator feature' under agreed functions.
'Large accessible buttons for core functions'.
'Hidden/less prominent secondary functions' and 'Secondary/advanced functions hidden or less prominent, possibly behind a sliding panel'.
'Secondary/advanced functions hidden or less prominent'.

Notes say a rechargeable cradle was 'proposed' and list 'Rechargeable or long-life battery solution'; the PM said 'that's a good idea, we'll keep it', so the notes leave it as an open option rather than a decision.
'Target group: broad appeal, roughly under 65; age segmentation less useful...' reflects the target-group discussion.
'Voice recognition ruled out: too expensive, not essential for a remote'.
'Chip quality critical for clean signal transmission' touches it, but the question of making infrared more functional (battery, chip, component quality) is not presented as a discussed issue.
'Energy source (battery or rechargeable cradle)', 'Rechargeable cradle ... proposed as alternative to disposable batteries', 'Rechargeable or long-life battery solution'.

errors.claim: Working design presentation not yet on the server; save from email into shared folder.
errors.why_wrong: The industrial designer's working design presentation was in the shared folder; it was the project manager's presentation that was only in email and not on the server.

errors.claim: age segmentation less useful than lifestyle/attitude targeting
errors.why_wrong: Nobody proposed lifestyle/attitude targeting; the transcript shows an income-group idea and then the PM's conclusion to define objectives (fashion, simplicity) instead of a target group.
